item.title: Hadron 1.0.2
item.description:
• Runtime downloads show a progress bar with megabytes and a percentage, and can be stopped. Before, the download said 0% until it had finished.
  • Wine 11.19 for Apple Silicon can be downloaded. It runs x86 games with FEX instead of Rosetta and needs macOS 26.5.
  • The Update and Repair rows say which Hadron is installed for Steam and which this app brings.
  • A new build of Hadron no longer shows as an update when only the signatures of its helper programs changed.
  • A supported runtime that is not on this Mac and cannot be downloaded yet keeps a row that says so, instead of vanishing from the list.

item.title: Hadron 1.0.1
item.description:
The first release with automatic updates.

  • Updates: Hadron is signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updates itself through Sparkle. Hadron → Check for Updates… works.
  • Runtime downloads: Wine 11.15, Wine Staging 11.15, Wine 11.19 and CrossOver Wine 26.3 can be downloaded from the Status page, checked and set up in one step. CrossOver's download comes without D3DMetal; Add D3DMetal… takes it from Apple's Game Porting Toolkit or CrossOver on your Mac.
  • Launch window: while a game starts, a small window shows each step, the game's Windows processes, both logs, and a warning when nothing happens for 30 seconds, with Stop Game and Save Diagnostics. The Launches section keeps recent launches.
  • Controllers: Steam Input's virtual pad reaches games, with its buttons in the right order. Before, games under every runtime saw no controller.
  • Steam's permissions: Steam keeps its input and device permissions across Hadron updates, because Hadron signs it with a stable identity of its own instead of ad hoc.
  • Switching runtimes: a game's prefix moves between the Rosetta and Apple Silicon runtimes in place, instead of asking for a rebuild. Moving back to CrossOver works too.
  • Apple Silicon: Ubisoft Connect, and with it Trackmania, starts under FEX.
  • Open Steam in the toolbar and the Setup menu, a new icon, and the Status page follows Steam quitting and starting.
